Interface ISenderReceiverDataMapping

  • All Superinterfaces:
    IDataMapping, IHasModelObject, IModelAbstraction

    @PublishedApi(value=ADDITIONS_ALLOWED)
 @PublishedApiDomain(value=AUTOMATION_IF)
public interface ISenderReceiverDataMapping
extends IDataMapping
    ISenderReceiverDataMapping represents the mapping of an IDataCommunicationElement to an ISignalInstance or ISignalGroupInstance.

      • getChildDataMappings

        @PublishedMethod
<T extends ISenderReceiverDataMapping> java.util.List<T> getChildDataMappings()
        Retrieves the child mappings for the next hierarchy level. Please check getLeafDataMappings(), for most use cases it is the better choice, because it evaluates the whole hierarchy of a data mapping. It also provides an example.
        Returns:
        The child mappings of a complex data mapping or an empty list when not applicable.

      • getLeafDataMappings

        @PublishedMethod
java.util.List<ISenderReceiverDataMapping> getLeafDataMappings()
        This is the method you call if you need to know the mapped communication elements for all signals of a complex data mapping.

        Scans the whole hierarchy below this ISenderReceiverDataMapping and collects all mappings that actually map a data element to a system signal. That means this methods ignores the composite mappings (SenderRecCompositeTypeMapping) which are only used to define structure and returns only data mappings that really reference a system signal.

        Example:
        We have a record 'MyRecord' with a record element 'MyRecElement' which is an array.
        'MyRecord' is mapped to the system signal group 'MySignalGroup'.
        The array element at index [0] of 'MyRecElement' is mapped to group signal 'MyGroupSignal1' and the array element at index [1] is mapped to group signal 'MyGroupSignal2'.

        So the complex data mapping looks like this:
        'MyRecord' -> 'MySignalGroup': Maps the record to the signal group (root mapping).
        'MyRecord.MyRecElement' -> null: This mapping does only define the structure.
        'MyRecord.MyRecElement[0]' -> 'MySignalGroup.MyGroupSignal1' -> First leaf mapping.
        'MyRecord.MyRecElement[1]' -> 'MySignalGroup.MyGroupSignal2' -> Second leaf mapping.

        Returns:
        The leaf mappings of a complex data mapping or an empty list when not applicable.
